conclusions.metric_scale: Calibrated stereo supplies metric camera-axis depth. The recorder explicitly uses calibrated translations and stores meters; zero depth remains unknown.
conclusions.intrinsics: Per-frame intrinsics describe ray directions and pixel scale, but intrinsics alone cannot resolve absolute scale from RGB.
conclusions.backprojection: X=(u-cx)*Z/fx, Y=(v-cy)*Z/fy, Z=saved depth_m. Coordinates use the undistorted aligned RGB camera frame.
conclusions.existing_oak: output/site-splat-20261026/oak-snapshot already has metric Gaussian means from saved depth. Rendered new-view depth is inferred geometry, not another sensor measurement.
conclusions.rgb_reconstruction: Proposed extension, not implemented: identify corresponding static points in SfM and synchronized OAK data, reject invalid/edge/outlier depth, robustly estimate meters-per-reconstruction-unit, and verify scale across views and a measured reference. Scale both point positions and camera translations consistently; Gaussian sizes scale too.
conclusions.old_site: The phone-only Arrowbrook reconstruction has no corresponding recorded OAK observations and remains arbitrary-scale. OAK hardware elsewhere cannot retrospectively scale it without shared landmarks or another measured reference.
conclusions.turtle: Depth helps estimate visible-shell extent but does not reveal hidden anatomy. Use masks and valid interior depth; bounding boxes may contain background.
conclusions.uncertainty: Metric units do not establish metrological accuracy. Luxonis published depth accuracy uses controlled textured targets and is not a guarantee for grass, shell edges, motion or distant targets.
conclusions.point_cloud_bounds: PointCloudData exposes min/max axis-aligned bounds in configured units. Object dimensions require selecting object points first; whole-scene bounds are not shell dimensions. Camera-axis extents depend on object pose and visible support.
